questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which choice best defines tone in speech communication?

answer.text: A. The attitude a speaker communicates through word choice and delivery

feedback.text: Correct. Tone is the attitude the audience hears through the speaker's language, voice, and delivery choices.

answer.text: B. The number of slides used in a presentation

feedback.text: This confuses tone with presentation materials. Slides may support a speech, but tone comes from the speaker's attitude and language.

answer.text: C. The exact place where the speech happens

feedback.text: This describes setting, not tone. Setting may affect choices, but tone is how the message sounds to the audience.

answer.text: D. The amount of time the speaker is allowed to talk

feedback.text: This describes time limit, not tone. A speaker can use an appropriate or inappropriate tone in any amount of time.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

A speaker is explaining a project to classmates. Which tone is most appropriate?

answer.text: A. Angry and insulting

feedback.text: This would make classmates defensive and distract from the message. A speaker should use a tone that helps the audience understand.

answer.text: B. Confusing and careless

feedback.text: This does not support communication. A class presentation needs clear language and a focused tone.

answer.text: C. Clear, respectful, and confident

feedback.text: Correct. This tone supports understanding, keeps the audience engaged, and shows that the speaker is prepared.

answer.text: D. Secretive and vague

feedback.text: This prevents the audience from understanding the message. Audience-aware speakers make their ideas clear.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which sentence best fits a formal email to a teacher?

answer.text: A. I need you to fix my grade today.

feedback.text: This sounds demanding and does not fit the audience. A formal message should make a respectful request.

answer.text: B. Could we please discuss my grade when you are available?

feedback.text: Correct. This sentence is respectful, clear, and appropriate for communicating with a teacher.

answer.text: C. My grade is bad and this is annoying.

feedback.text: This expresses frustration but does not make a clear or respectful request. Tone should support the purpose.

answer.text: D. Fix this because I do not like it.

feedback.text: This is too demanding. Audience-aware communication uses respectful language, especially with school staff.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.05

Which sentence uses the most precise academic vocabulary?

answer.text: A. The thing happened because of some stuff.

feedback.text: This is vague. Academic vocabulary should name the idea clearly so the audience can follow the explanation.

answer.text: B. The reason is just obvious to everyone.

feedback.text: This avoids precise explanation. Academic speaking should explain the reason with clear words.

answer.text: C. It did what it did because that is how it works.

feedback.text: This repeats unclear language. Replace vague words with specific terms tied to the topic.

answer.text: D. The outcome changed because the evidence showed a different pattern.

feedback.text: Correct. This sentence uses precise academic vocabulary such as outcome, evidence, and pattern.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

A student says to a group member, "That part of the presentation is terrible." Which revision best improves tone?

answer.text: A. That part is terrible, but I am saying it nicely.

feedback.text: This still uses insulting language. A respectful tone focuses on the work and offers a useful next step.

answer.text: B. This section may need clearer evidence. Can we revise it together?

feedback.text: Correct. This revision identifies the issue, keeps the tone respectful, and invites collaboration.

answer.text: C. I do not like it, so delete it.

feedback.text: This is too forceful and does not explain the communication problem. Good feedback gives a reason.

answer.text: D. Everyone will dislike your part.

feedback.text: This attacks the person and predicts audience reaction without support. Tone should help the group improve.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which presentation opening gives the audience the clearest focus?

answer.text: A. Today I will explain three ways speakers adjust tone for different audiences.

feedback.text: Correct. This opening states the topic and previews the organization, which helps the audience follow the presentation.

answer.text: B. I am going to talk for a while about several things.

feedback.text: This is too vague. The audience needs a clear topic and direction.

answer.text: C. I found some information, but I am not sure what it means yet.

feedback.text: This weakens the focus. A prepared speaker should guide the audience with a clear purpose.

answer.text: D. Before I begin, here is an unrelated story from last week.

feedback.text: This may distract the audience unless it connects directly to the presentation focus.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Why should a speaker consider purpose before choosing voice and tone?

answer.text: A. Purpose tells the speaker which words to avoid saying at all times.

feedback.text: This is too absolute. Purpose guides word choice, but it does not create one fixed list for every situation.

answer.text: B. Purpose matters only for written essays, not speech.

feedback.text: This is incorrect. Purpose matters whenever a person communicates, including speaking and presenting.

answer.text: C. Purpose lets the speaker ignore the audience's needs.

feedback.text: This reverses the lesson concept. Purpose and audience work together to shape effective communication.

answer.text: D. Purpose helps the speaker decide whether to inform, persuade, request, or discuss.

feedback.text: Correct. When the purpose is clear, the speaker can choose a tone and voice that fit the communication goal.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which message best matches a respectful tone for asking a classmate to speak more quietly?

answer.text: A. Stop being loud because you are ruining everything.

feedback.text: This sounds accusatory. A respectful request should name the need without attacking the person.

answer.text: B. You always talk too much and never listen.

feedback.text: This uses blaming language. Tone improves when the speaker focuses on the current need.

answer.text: C. Could you lower your voice a little so I can focus on the task?

feedback.text: Correct. This message is clear, respectful, and connected to the purpose of staying focused.

answer.text: D. I guess you can keep talking if you want to bother everyone.

feedback.text: This is sarcastic. Sarcasm often harms collaboration and weakens the message.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.05

Which word choice best supports academic communication in a presentation?

answer.text: A. evidence

feedback.text: Correct. Evidence is an academic word that helps a speaker explain how a claim is supported.

answer.text: B. stuff

feedback.text: This is too vague. Academic communication uses precise vocabulary so the audience understands the point.

answer.text: C. whatever

feedback.text: This sounds careless and unclear. It does not help explain an idea to an academic audience.

answer.text: D. thingy

feedback.text: This is informal and imprecise. A presenter should choose words that clearly name the idea.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which closing best supports a coherent oral presentation?

answer.text: A. That is all. I forgot the rest.

feedback.text: This does not reinforce the message. A strong closing should help the audience remember the main idea.

answer.text: B. In conclusion, audience, purpose, voice, and tone work together to make communication effective.

feedback.text: Correct. This closing restates the focus and connects the main lesson ideas clearly.

answer.text: C. I am done because the timer stopped.

feedback.text: This ends the speech but does not summarize the message. A closing should support understanding.

answer.text: D. My slides were about many different topics.

feedback.text: This is vague and does not show coherent focus. The audience needs a clear final takeaway.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

A speaker wants to persuade classmates to join a service project. Which tone would likely work best?

answer.text: A. Bored and uncertain

feedback.text: This tone would weaken the message. Persuasion usually needs energy and confidence.

answer.text: B. Harsh and demanding

feedback.text: This may push classmates away. Persuasive communication should still respect the audience.

answer.text: C. Encouraging and confident

feedback.text: Correct. This tone supports persuasion by showing belief in the idea while respecting classmates.

answer.text: D. Confused and hesitant

feedback.text: This makes the purpose unclear. A persuasive speaker should present the message with clear confidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which question should a speaker ask first when adjusting tone?

answer.text: A. Who is my audience, and what is my purpose?

feedback.text: Correct. Audience and purpose guide the speaker's choices about formality, voice, detail, and tone.

answer.text: B. How can I make the message sound the most dramatic?

feedback.text: This may distract from the purpose. Tone should fit the audience and goal, not just sound dramatic.

answer.text: C. How can I use the fewest words possible?

feedback.text: Being concise can help, but it is not the first question. The speaker must understand audience and purpose first.

answer.text: D. Which words will make me sound smarter than everyone else?

feedback.text: This focuses on impressing rather than communicating. Academic vocabulary should clarify ideas, not show off.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.05

Which sentence best uses academic vocabulary without sounding confusing?

answer.text: A. The topic is basically a bunch of things about talking.

feedback.text: This is too vague. Academic vocabulary should make the topic clearer.

answer.text: B. The communication thing has many pieces and stuff.

feedback.text: This uses imprecise words. Replace thing and stuff with exact terms.

answer.text: C. The speaker used fancy terminology to demonstrate superiority.

feedback.text: This may sound formal, but it does not clearly explain the lesson idea in student-friendly academic language.

answer.text: D. The speaker adjusted tone to match the audience and purpose.

feedback.text: Correct. This sentence uses precise vocabulary from the lesson while staying clear.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which statement shows the strongest understanding of voice?

answer.text: A. Voice means speaking louder than everyone else.

feedback.text: This confuses voice with volume. Voice includes the speaker's style, word choice, and way of expressing the message.

answer.text: B. Voice is the speaker's style or presence in the message.

feedback.text: Correct. Voice is how the speaker comes across through language, organization, and delivery choices.

answer.text: C. Voice means using slang in every situation.

feedback.text: This is too limited and often inappropriate. Voice should fit the audience and purpose.

answer.text: D. Voice means avoiding all personality when speaking.

feedback.text: This is incorrect. Voice can show personality while still being appropriate for the context.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which choice best supports logical organization in a speech?

answer.text: A. Place ideas randomly so the audience stays surprised.

feedback.text: This makes the speech harder to follow. Organization should help the audience understand.

answer.text: B. Repeat the same point without adding support.

feedback.text: This does not build the message. Logical organization develops ideas with support.

answer.text: C. Arrange ideas in an order that helps the audience follow the main point.

feedback.text: Correct. A coherent speech has a clear order that supports the speaker's focus.

answer.text: D. Skip transitions because the audience can guess the connections.

feedback.text: This creates confusion. Transitions help listeners understand how ideas connect.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

A student is speaking to younger students about hallway safety. Which tone is most appropriate?

answer.text: A. Sarcastic and annoyed

feedback.text: This would not help younger students learn. The tone should support understanding and cooperation.

answer.text: B. Overly technical and confusing

feedback.text: This does not fit younger students. Audience awareness requires language they can understand.

answer.text: C. Silent and unsure

feedback.text: This does not communicate the safety message clearly. The speaker needs a confident, helpful tone.

answer.text: D. Friendly, clear, and firm

feedback.text: Correct. This tone fits younger students because it is understandable, respectful, and serious enough for a safety topic.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which revision best changes an informal message into a more formal request?

answer.text: A. May I please have a few minutes to explain my concern?

feedback.text: Correct. This revision uses polite wording and a formal tone that fits a respectful request.

answer.text: B. I need to talk now, so listen.

feedback.text: This is demanding. A formal request should respect the listener's time and role.

answer.text: C. Hey, I have a problem or whatever.

feedback.text: This is too casual and unclear. Formal communication should be precise and respectful.

answer.text: D. You should already know what I want.

feedback.text: This is unclear and accusatory. The speaker should state the request directly.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.05

Why is precise vocabulary important in speech communication?

answer.text: A. It lets the speaker avoid explaining ideas.

feedback.text: This is incorrect. Precise vocabulary should support explanation, not replace it.

answer.text: B. It allows the speaker to use words the audience cannot understand.

feedback.text: This works against communication. Good vocabulary choices clarify meaning for the audience.

answer.text: C. It makes every speech sound formal even when formal tone is wrong.

feedback.text: This overstates the idea. Vocabulary should match audience and purpose.

answer.text: D. It helps the audience understand exactly what the speaker means.

feedback.text: Correct. Precise words reduce confusion and make the message easier to follow.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which presentation plan best connects evidence to a main idea?

answer.text: A. Give evidence first and never explain what it proves.

feedback.text: This leaves the audience to guess. Evidence should be connected to the main idea.

answer.text: B. State a main idea but give no supporting details.

feedback.text: This is incomplete. A presentation needs support that develops the focus.

answer.text: C. State the main idea, present evidence, and explain how the evidence supports the idea.

feedback.text: Correct. This structure helps the audience understand both the claim and the support.

answer.text: D. Use evidence that is unrelated because it sounds interesting.

feedback.text: This weakens the presentation. Evidence should be relevant to the main idea.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which speaker choice best shows audience awareness?

answer.text: A. Using the same tone for a friend, teacher, and principal

feedback.text: This ignores audience differences. A speaker should adjust tone for different listeners.

answer.text: B. Choosing words only because they sound impressive

feedback.text: This may confuse the audience. Word choice should support understanding.

answer.text: C. Speaking without considering why the message matters

feedback.text: This ignores purpose. Audience awareness includes understanding why the speaker is communicating.

answer.text: D. Adjusting formality, detail, and tone to fit the listener and purpose

feedback.text: Correct. This choice shows that the speaker is thinking about both audience and purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Read the comment: "Whatever. Your plan is fine, I guess." What is the main tone problem?

answer.text: A. It sounds dismissive and does not support collaboration.

feedback.text: Correct. Words like whatever and I guess can make the speaker sound uninterested or disrespectful.

answer.text: B. It is too formal for a group discussion.

feedback.text: This is not the main issue. The sentence is informal, but the bigger problem is its dismissive tone.

answer.text: C. It gives too much evidence.

feedback.text: This sentence gives no evidence. The issue is tone and lack of useful response.

answer.text: D. It explains the idea too carefully.

feedback.text: This sentence does not explain the idea. It gives a weak and unclear response.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which sentence best shows a respectful disagreement?

answer.text: A. That answer is bad, and you should stop saying it.

feedback.text: This attacks the person and does not explain the disagreement. Respectful disagreement focuses on ideas.

answer.text: B. I see it differently because the example points to another conclusion.

feedback.text: Correct. This sentence disagrees respectfully and gives a reason connected to evidence.

answer.text: C. You are wrong, and I am obviously right.

feedback.text: This is disrespectful and does not support the claim. Tone matters when disagreeing.

answer.text: D. I disagree, but I will not explain why.

feedback.text: This is incomplete. A respectful disagreement should include reasoning when possible.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which choice best describes a coherent focus?

answer.text: A. A speech that changes topics every few seconds

feedback.text: This lacks focus. Coherence means the ideas connect to one main message.

answer.text: B. A speech that includes every fact the speaker found

feedback.text: This can overwhelm the audience. Coherent focus requires selecting details that support the point.

answer.text: C. A speech where each part supports the main idea

feedback.text: Correct. Coherent focus means the introduction, support, and conclusion all connect to the same purpose.

answer.text: D. A speech with no introduction because the audience can guess the topic

feedback.text: This makes the focus harder to follow. An introduction helps orient the audience.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.05

Which revision replaces vague language with precise academic language?

answer.text: A. The speaker talked about some stuff.

feedback.text: This remains vague. The audience still does not know what the speaker explained.

answer.text: B. The speaker did a thing with words.

feedback.text: This is still unclear. Academic communication requires specific wording.

answer.text: C. The speaker was, like, really good at talking.

feedback.text: This is informal and imprecise. It does not name the skill being discussed.

answer.text: D. The speaker used evidence to support the main claim.

feedback.text: Correct. This revision uses precise academic vocabulary and clearly describes the communication skill.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L02_Quiz_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which statement best summarizes Lesson 2?

answer.text: A. Effective speakers match audience, purpose, voice, and tone.

feedback.text: Correct. This is the central lesson idea: speakers make choices based on who is listening and why they are communicating.

answer.text: B. Effective speakers always use the most formal tone possible.

feedback.text: This is too rigid. Formal tone is useful in some situations, but tone must match the audience and purpose.

answer.text: C. Effective speakers ignore audience so the message stays personal.

feedback.text: This contradicts the lesson. Audience awareness is essential for effective communication.

answer.text: D. Effective speakers use academic words even when the audience cannot understand them.

feedback.text: This misuses academic vocabulary. Word choice should clarify the message for the audience.
